$comment: Frameless colour system, REBUILT from brand/_source/concept/CONCEPT-ART-AUTHORITATIVE.jpeg. AGENTS: read `lime_law` before you use #cce007 anywhere, and read `depth_law` before you build any surface. Every ratio here is computed with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula and is re-derivable from the hex pair beside it; brand/tools/structural-gate.mjs recomputes all of them.

meta.organizing_idea: Saturated, cool, physical. Vivid die-cut stickers with a real drop shadow, laid on a dark textured bed. Colour is used in confident blocks — never desaturated, never aged.
meta.how_values_were_obtained: Real pixels, sampled in Chromium by drawing the concept art to a canvas and reading getImageData. Two statistics per region: the block average (what a naive sample gives, and what gets pulled toward the cream band and the paper grain) and the mean of the top 5% most saturated pixels (what the fill actually is). Every framework fill below is anchored on the SATURATED statistic — anchoring on the block average is the exact error that produced the rejected first attempt.
meta.supersedes: The pre-rebuild palette (#f2efd4 / #1d2c22 / #fdf8e4 / #ebd5a0), which was measured from a generated stand-in rather than from the concept art. It was desaturated, green-shifted and warm. The real art is cooler, bluer, brighter and saturated.
meta.default_bed_is_dark: The kit defaults to the DARK bed. Saturated colour needs a dark ground to read as lit, all three named references (avara.xyz, react.gg, sticker.oooo.so) are dark, and lime display type is only legal on dark. A light paper island is available with [data-surface="light"] for reading-length copy.
meta.pure_white_rule: #ffffff is FORBIDDEN as a page bed. It is permitted INSIDE a saturated framework sticker, where it is the name label and carries a measured ratio against that fill.

lime_law.one_sentence: Lime is a surface, a mark and a display voice. Never an ink on light.
lime_law.why: #cce007 has a relative luminance of 0.6616 — it is a LIGHT colour that behaves like a highlighter. It cannot carry reading copy on any light bed, at any size, in any weight.
lime_law.still_true_after_the_rebuild: This rule survived the rebuild intact. It was never a taste call: lime on light genuinely fails, and it fails by a factor of three. What changed around it is that the kit now defaults to a dark bed, so the surface where lime is legal is the common case rather than the exception.

rules.body_text_on_light: NEVER. Any light surface, any size, any weight.
rules.body_text_on_dark: Avoid. Legal by ratio, wrong by role — reading copy is --ink cream. Lime is for display and for marks.
rules.display_text: Legal on --surface (dark) at 12.41:1, at --step-3 or larger. This is where the hero headline lives.
rules.button_fill: Primary CTA = lime fill + --accent-ink label (13.08:1). The flagship usage of the colour.
rules.the_wordmark: The lime wordmark fill is a FILL, not type in the accessibility sense — it is ringed by a black keyline and a cream band and carries a drop shadow, and its accessible name comes from the surrounding markup. Do not "fix" its contrast by changing the fill.
rules.framework_marks: A framework logo may NEVER render in --accent. Marks render in that project's own brand colours, in white, or as the grey silhouette used for the deselected carousel state. Nothing else.

measured_failures.context: lime on the light paper island
lime on the cream die-cut band

depth_law.one_sentence: Every die-cut object casts a real shadow. Elevation is the brand.
depth_law.why: The most defining quality of the concept art is depth — the wordmark and all six badges sit above the page on a heavy offset shadow. The previous version of this kit BANNED box-shadow kit-wide, having measured four flat vector PNGs and generalised from them. That deleted the one thing the art is most recognisable for.
depth_law.the_stack_outward: fill -> tinted dark keyline -> thick band (6-8% of width) -> drop shadow
depth_law.use_drop_shadow_not_box_shadow: filter: drop-shadow() EVERYWHERE. box-shadow casts a shadow of the element's BOX — a rounded rectangle behind a die-cut shape, which instantly kills the illusion. drop-shadow() follows the actual alpha silhouette: the cut edge, the lettering, the wobble of the band. Stack two of them (a hard offset plus a soft ambient) for the register the concept art's wordmark reads in.
depth_law.where_the_shadow_goes: On the element that owns the alpha — the PNG, the SVG, or the outermost die-cut wrapper. A filter on a parent shadows the whole subtree as ONE silhouette, which is right for a sticker and never right for a text block.
depth_law.the_one_box_shadow: --elev-inset, and only that. A filter can only draw outside an alpha silhouette, never inside it, so a well cut INTO the page has no drop-shadow equivalent.
depth_law.filter_side_effects: A non-none filter creates a stacking context AND a containing block for fixed/absolute descendants. A position: fixed child of a filtered element is fixed to that element, not to the viewport — this matters for any slide-in panel.
depth_law.texture: The page bed is NEVER a flat fill. A fine noise grain is applied globally, with an optional faint ruled grid. See ./elevation.css.

--surface.intent: The default page bed, and it is DARK. A deep teal-black in the same family as the "COMPILED OUTPUTS" chip in the concept art, which is the art's own piece of UI.
--surface.measured_as: the dark green-black of the concept art's tag chip (top-5%-saturation sample #011c0d), opened up until cream reading copy clears AA comfortably
--surface.never: Never #ffffff, and never flat. A page bed with no texture is the failure the owner named directly.

--surface-raised.intent: Cards, detail panels, the carousel stage. It is only 1.12:1 against the bed on purpose — a raised panel is separated by its SHADOW and its band, not by a value step.
--surface-raised.derived_from: --surface lightened along the same teal-black hue line

--surface-sunk.intent: Code wells, and anything that should read as cut INTO the page rather than laid on it. Pair with an inset shadow, never an outer one.

--ink.intent: All reading copy. On the dark bed a bright cool cream; on the light paper island a near-black with a faint green cast.
--ink.measured_as: the concept art's die-cut band cream #e0dfca, brightened for type

--ink-muted.intent: Captions, metadata, spec-table labels. Not reading copy at body length.

--accent.intent: The lime. Display type on dark, primary button fills, the wordmark fill, the outer focus ring. Governed entirely by `lime_law`.
--accent.measured_as: the concept art measures #c7da00 at peak saturation; the owner's canonical #cce007 is correct and JPEG averaging is what pulls the sample down
--accent.never: Never a framework logo. Never reading copy.

--accent-ink.role: the label on a lime fill
--accent-ink.intent: The one ink that goes on lime. Fixed — it does NOT flip with the surface, because a lime fill is a light surface wherever it appears.

--accent-cool.role: the accent that CAN be an ink
--accent-cool.intent: Links, inline emphasis, secondary emphasis — anywhere you wanted accent colour on TEXT. This token exists precisely because lime cannot be an ink; without it the palette reads as monochrome plus a highlighter.
--accent-cool.measured_as: the concept art's sky cyan (#73b3bf top-5% sample), brightened for the dark bed and deepened for the light island

--band.intent: The thick cream band ringing a die-cut object — the paper it was cut from. Neutral cream is for the WORDMARK; framework stickers tint their band to their own hue (see `framework_colors`).
--band.measured_as: the wordmark band in the concept art
--band.never: Never a page bed, and never a text colour on light.
--band.geometry: 6-8% of the object's width. Chunky. See ./sticker.css.

--keyline.role: the drawn edge of a die-cut object
--keyline.intent: The heavy near-black stroke between a fill and its band. Neutral black is correct for the WORDMARK, which is what the art shows; framework stickers use the dark end of their own hue instead.
--keyline.measured_as: the wordmark keyline in the concept art (darkest sample #010000)

--warning.intent: Coming-soon tags and in-progress states. FILL ONLY on light, always with an --accent-ink label.

--silhouette.intent: The grey a framework sticker collapses to when another is selected. It must lose colour ENTIRELY rather than merely dim — that total loss is what makes the selected sticker read as lit, and it is the mechanic avara.xyz is built on.
--silhouette.derived_from: avara.xyz rest/selected states, studied in a browser

--silhouette-band.intent: The band of a desaturated sticker. Grey, not cream — a cream band on a grey fill still reads as a live sticker.

--focus-inner.intent: Carries the indicator contrast on light and on any saturated fill.

--focus-outer.intent: Carries the indicator contrast on dark.

framework_colors.$comment: Six frameworks, six saturated fills — the die-cut sticker colours from the concept art, anchored on the top-5%-saturation sample rather than the block average. The logo colours are each project's own; Frameless does not own them and states them here only so a badge can be built without a network request.
framework_colors.construction: saturated fill (glossy, lighter at top-left) -> keyline in the dark end of that hue -> band tinted to that hue -> drop shadow -> about -3deg of tilt
framework_colors.name_label: The framework name is set in white INSIDE the sticker, always. Not a tooltip, not a caption. A word is the only treatment that survives a crop, a grayscale conversion and a screenshot with no alt text.

surface_flip.how: Put [data-surface="light"] on a region for the light paper island; [data-surface="deep"] switches back. The role tokens flip as a SET.
surface_flip.why_as_a_set: Flipping one at a time is how the dark-bed cream ink ends up on the light paper at 1.1:1 — invisible, and the single most expensive mistake available. Both failure directions are listed in forbidden_pairs so the gate proves they are real.
surface_flip.why_those_do_not_flip: They are printed ink and printed paper, not roles. A die-cut band is the same cream on any bed, and a React sticker is the same blue on any bed. That is what makes a sticker a physical object rather than a themed div.

computation.large_text_token_gate: --step-2 and above clears the WCAG large-text threshold at every viewport in the shipped Utopia scale, so size gating is expressed as a TOKEN and stays checkable.
computation.verified_by: brand/tools/structural-gate.mjs recomputes every ratio in this file from its own hex pair.
